transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-02
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 1:15
Attendees: Alex Martinez, Priya Shah, Ben Carter, Nina Alvarez, Tamara Ortiz, Ethan Wu, Sarah Kim, Liam O'Connor

Summary:
Quick sync to validate Q4 launch readiness for the upcoming roadmap tranche: focus areas - canary/rollout, infra capacity, incident/playbook, and security/compliance handoff. Agreed on owners and short deadlines.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: alright everyone, thanks for being here. I think we've got about 75 minutes so we'll go through the checklist, infra signoffs, canary plan, and then security/compliance notes, any blockers. uh, can I get a quick ack on who we have?
[00:10] Priya: Priya here, SE, I'll cover canary and rollout details.
[00:15] Ben: Ben, infrastructure, running the load tests and autoscaler configs.
[00:20] Nina: Nina, product ops, I'll handle the launch checklist and comms.
[00:25] Tamara: Tamara here, product - high level ownership.
[00:30] Ethan: Ethan, platform director, infra questions are for me.
[00:35] Sarah: Sarah, eng manager for serving runtime.
[00:40] Liam: Liam, reliability lead, I'll keep an eye on SRE runbooks.

[01:05] Alex: cool. first item: launch checklist. Nina can you run through the gaps we saw last week?
[01:15] Nina: yeah, sure. so items outstanding: incident playbook isn't merged into the checklist, we have ambiguous owners for DB failover steps, and the monitoring dashboards need a final pass - some panels reference old metric names like redwood.requests_per_min which is, uh, slightly off. also the legal sign-off on data retention needs to be in place.
[01:45] Tamara: for data retention, are we talking the Hosted API defaults or Dedicated/private customers specific settings?
[01:50] Nina: good point. for this launch tranche it's focused on Dedicated customers but we need the wording so that Private deployments are covered too.
[02:05] Sarah: quick note: the KV cache metrics we added last sprint are live on canary, but there are a couple of spikes during long context loads, might be normal but flagged.

[03:00] Alex: okay, let's mark action items: Nina will incorporate incident runbook, Ben will run a more extensive load test, Ethan to confirm autoscaler SLOs.

[03:25] Priya: on canary/rollout: my proposed plan is a staged rollout over 72 hours with percentage ramping - 1% to 25% to 50% to 100% - each step gated on latency p50/p95 and error budget burn. we should also have a fallback model variant that is quantized to a lower-cost profile if latency exceeds thresholds.
[04:00] Ben: do we have capacity for that ramp in Dedicated? I need to confirm reserved pool plus burst. current numbers show we can hit 25% easily but 50% might need burst GPUs or spillover to hosted.
[04:20] Ethan: we can allow spillover to hosted as a fallback but we need to ensure routing policy is set so no customer data leaks - route only to verified model variants and region pinned. also update KV cache warmup to avoid cold starts at each ramp.
[04:50] Priya: yep, route policy and privacy are key. I'll draft the routing config and fallback policy, include region pinning and SLO thresholds.

[05:30] Alex: there was a question from legal on audit logs and KMS rotation - do we have an owner to confirm rotation windows?
[05:40] Nina: I can own the coordination with security, but Ethan you'll need to confirm the technical rotation window for KMS/HSM on the private deployments.
[05:50] Ethan: yes, confirmable. default is 90 days for keys but we can support more aggressive rotation for specific accounts. will confirm by 9/11.

[06:20] Liam: small note from SRE - we should define clear rollback criteria beyond just error rate, like token-level timeout percent and KV cache miss rates. otherwise we might flip too late.
[06:35] Sarah: agreed, add KV cache miss threshold of 5% and token timeouts > 800ms for >5 minutes as a trigger.

[07:10] Ben: on the load tests - I propose two phases: synthetic throughput run (24 hours) and then a production shadow during a low-traffic window. synthetic will validate autoscaler behavior and memory leak detection.
[07:35] Priya: for shadow traffic, can we ensure no actual customer PII is routed; use sanitized payloads? we don't want any legal concerns.
[07:50] Ethan: yes, use sanitized payload generation. Security will sign off on the dataset.

[08:15] Alex: regarding monitoring - we need a runbook for paging wiht clear escalation steps, and a playbook entry for degraded quality (model regressions). Priya, Sarah, can you own drafting that?
[08:30] Sarah: yeah, I'll handle the runbook template and escalation chain.
[08:35] Priya: I'll add the model-quality checks and prompt set guards.

[09:00] Tamara: any blockers on dependencies? models are green, infra needs the autoscaler confirmation and load test results, legal needs the retention language. seems like three short sprints.

[09:20] Alex: timing - we want to start the canary on 2026-09-20 and full rollout by 2026-09-27 if things look good. that gives two weeks to finish checks. deadlines will be in action items.

[10:00] Nina: quick note on comms - we should prepare a launch note for customers and internal ops runbook, also schedule a pre-launch war room the day before.
[10:15] Liam: war room should include on-call SRE, SE, product ops, and a legal contact on standby.

[10:40] Alex: security review - any outstanding items from the last security review?
[10:50] Nina: the big one was audit logging retention and encryption at rest for private deployments. legal asked for a short doc summarizing KMS behavior and audit trail retention config. I have a draft, will share the link in the notes.
[11:10] Priya: also, we need to validate that our fallback to hosted endpoints does not violate the VPC-only requirement for some enterprise customers. fallback should be opt-in per account.
[11:25] Ethan: agreed. per-account routing flags will be respected; default is no-hosted-fallback for VPC-only accounts. we'll update the routing policy.

[12:00] Ben: one more infra note - when we do the synthetic test, watch for KV cache eviction churn; if we see >20% eviction churn we should raise the cache size and consider sticky routing.
[12:20] Sarah: noted. also let's double-check the kernel selection heuristics for long sequences - some models switch to fallback kernel that increases latency. we need profiler traces from the canary to validate.

[13:00] Alex: ok this is great. let's run through a quick recap of owners and deadlines.
[13:10] Nina: I'll merge incident playbook into checklist and send by 2026-09-09.
[13:20] Ben: run 24h synthetic load test and schedule shadow test, results by 2026-09-15.
[13:30] Priya: draft routing/fallback policy and canary thresholds by 2026-09-12.
[13:40] Ethan: confirm autoscaler SLOs and KMS rotation windows by 2026-09-11.
[13:50] Sarah: compile runbook and escalation chain by 2026-09-12.
[14:00] Tamara: I'll own the final launch readiness signoff once those items are closed, target 2026-09-16 for pre-check.

[14:30] Alex: any other items?
[14:40] Priya: small ask - can we add one performance regression check into CI that runs the smallest smoke inference to detect obvious regressions? even if it's a mock.
[14:55] Ben: yes we can add a lightweight tracer run in CI.
[15:10] Alex: perfect. thanks everyone. I'll follow up with calendar invites for the pre-launch war room and a summary email with action items.

[15:30] End of call
